 THIS WRIT PETITION (CIVIL) HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 23.09.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 WP(C) NO. 27959 OF 2023  3  2024:KER:70645  JUDGMENT Dated this the 23rd day of September, 2024 The 1st petitioner claims to be a vendor of dry fish in the Chalakudy Market since 1978. The 1 st petitioner is occupying in Building No.FS28 as per valid license in ward No.XIX of the Chalakudy market complex on the basis of an agreement executed with the 2 nd respondent Municipality. The 2nd petitioner is the Merchants' Association and the 3rd petitioner claims to be the General Secretary of Merchants' Association. 
2. The allegation in the writ petition is that the 5 th respondent is carrying on illegal vending of dry fish on a cart in the Chalakudy market and despite the complainnt given to the Municipal authorities, no action has been taken to remove the 5 th respondent from the Chalakudy market inasmuch as the 5th respondent does not have any valid license to vend in the Chalakudy market.
The petitioners have approached this Court with the present writ petition seeking a writ of mandamus/direction commanding the Municipal authorities to remove all illegal traders from WP(C) NO. 27959 OF 2023 2024:KER:70645 Chalakudy market premises including the 5 th Joju M.L vs State Of Kerala on 23 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76234215/
2 respondent.
3. Sri. Sheejo Chacko, learned counsel for the Chalakudy Municipality submits that as per the interim order passed by this Court in W.P.(C.) No. 16905/2023 and connected one, action would have been taken against the 5th respondent and other persons who are vending illegally in the Chalakudy market. 
4. The learned counsel for the 5th respondent submits that the 5th respondent is a street vendor and he has been issued a license as a street vendor. However, the learned counsel for the 5 th respondent is not in a position to say that the 5th respondent has been allotted place in the Chalakudy market to vend dry fish. 
5. The learned counsel for the 5th respondent submits that this Court in W.P.(C.) No.27220/2013 vide judgment dated 23.01.2015, directed the respondent Municipality to identify a 'vending zone'
and complete the steps with regard to rehabilitation of the street vendors in accordance with the relevant provisions of law within a period of three months from the date of the judgment. However,
the Municipality has not taken WP(C) NO. 27959 OF 2023 2024:KER:70645 any steps to identify the vending zone for the street vendors like the 5th respondent, despite more than 9 years have elapsed since the judgment passed by this Court on 23.01.2015. 
6. He further submitted that the 5th respondent has filed connected W.P.(C.) No.16905/2023, with a prayer, not to take any action by the Municipal authorities against the street vending of the petitioner and also for the quashing of the order passed by the Ombudsman in Ext.P4, whereby the Municipality has been directed to evict the street vendors for illegally vending in the Chalakudy market.
7. The 5th respondent has also prayed for a direction to the Municipal authorities to take appropriate action to implement plan for street vending as per Section 21 read with first schedule and Promotional measures as per Section 31 of Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act in Chalakudy Municipality. When the 5th respondent does not have designated place allotted by the Municipality for carrying out his vending of dry fish in the Chalakudy market, the 5 th respondent WP(C) NO. 27959 OF 2023 2024:KER:70645 cannot be allowed to vend in the said market. In view thereof, the present writ petition is disposed of with direction to the respondents 1 to 4 to take appropriate measures for removal of the illegal vendors from the Chalakudy market and to protect the rights of vendors who have got designated place and license for vending in the market. Necessary action to be taken within period of fifteen days from today. 
Sd/-
